framework.name: STRATEGIC PRIORITY 3: HUMAN WELLBEING AND RESILIENCE
framework.description: WFP’s work under SP3 aims at enhancing the capacities of Government institutions to coordinate and manage food security and nutrition programmes, respond to shocks, address risks and vulnerabilities, enhance livelihoods and resilience of vulnerable populations across the life cycle as a contribution to SDG target 17.9. The Strategic Outcome is organised into two activities. The first is Activity 8. This is responsible for strengthening institutions and systems to deliver social protection programmes and is delivered through the Child Sensitive Social Protection Programme (CSSP). The second is activity 9 and this is charged with building the capacity of institutions to respond to shocks through the Strengthening Shock Responsive Systems in Karamoja (PRO-ACT) project.

projects.name: Refugees and other crisis affected people in Uganda have access to adequate nutritious food in times of crisis
projects.description: This focuses on providing critical food and nutrition assistance to refugees and food-insecure local populations in the Karamoja sub-region and Southwestern Uganda. Uganda experienced climatic shocks, and a continuous refugee influx, which contributed to increased needs. WFP partnered with stakeholders including the Government, UNHCR and cooperating partners, to improve food access, ensure that refugees receive adequate and nutritious food, and promote their financial inclusion. Additionally, food-insecure households in Karamoja benefited from early action interventions, providing both food assistance and nutrition support. WFP also extended food and cash assistance to communities affected by mudslides and floods in Kasese and Ntoroko districts.
projects.outcome: Output 3.1.1: Strengthened capacity of government and non-government institutions at national and sub national levels to effectively manage and deliver sustainable and inclusive quality social and protection services

projects.name: 3.1.1.1 Provide technical and financial support to government and non government actors to expand and sustainably provide  high impact food security and nutrition interventions for vulnerable and marginalised population especially adolescents and women of reproductive age in development and humanitarian situations
projects.description:
UNHCR
UNHCR
Achievements: The food security sector continues to contribute to Strategic Development Goal 2.1 by improving access to nutritious food among refugees and asylum seekers in the 13 refugee settlements in Uganda. Furthermore, the sector promotes the self-reliance of refugee communities through complimentary activities. The partners reached 1.39 million beneficiaries through the provision of in-kind food as well as cash-based transfers by the end of Q2. However, owing to the prioritization exercise conducted in July 2023, there was a reduction of 14% of beneficiaries who received in-kind assistance and 6% reduction in cash assistance. Additionally, the further reduction in in-kind rations in most refugee settlements due to limitations in funding increased cash enrolments since beneficiaries preferred cash to the reduced rations. Overall, the proportion of beneficiaries who received cash assistance increased from 60% to 63% from Q1 to Q4. 
Digital cash transfer mechanisms through agent banking continued to be scaled up, and cash beneficiaries owning bank accounts increased from 36 percent to 41 percent out of the overall total cash beneficiaries by the end of the year. To increase access to digital payment instruments, Mobile money will start in Kyangwali and Kiryandogo settlements. In addition to increasing access to digital payment instruments through agency banking, cash beneficiaries received financial literacy skills. A total of 2,954 beneficiaries were trained during the reporting period across all 13 settlements. Efforts to mitigate malnutrition continue to be strengthened through building the capacity of health workers, Village Health Teams (VHTs), and other community structures in providing Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) knowledge to promote better household nutrition. Similarly, active case findings have supported in managing the nutrition situation in the settlements. Currently, the recovery rate remains above the threshold with an average of 93% discharged as cured from the programme within the reporting period.
projects.outcome: Output 3.1.1: Strengthened capacity of government and non-government institutions at national and sub national levels to effectively manage and deliver sustainable and inclusive quality social and protection services

projects.name: 3.1.1.6 Provide technical and financial assistance to government and non-government actors to increase access  to gender inclusive and equitable health services including SRH, Mental Health, NCD prevention and control for all especially vulnerable and marginalised.
projects.description:
UNHCR
Achievements: In the Health Sector, the Under-5 mortality remained below the standard of <1.5/1,000. Mosquito net distribution, Indoor residual spraying (iRS) as well as Integrated community case management (iCCM) have ensured that mortalities are contained. Measles vaccination coverage was (83%) against the standard of 95% mainly due to vaccine stockouts as well as the increased number of new refugees. The consultations per clinician per day were higher for the Congolese (DRC) population (65) than for the South Sudan (SSD) population (40) than the acceptable standard of 50 consultations per clinician per day. During the reporting period, the health partners have identified and treated 7,874 children and 2,662 pregnant and lactating women for acute malnutrition, with a cure rate of 71.5%. The Refugee Population-based HIV Impact Assessment (RUPHIA) revealed the gains in HIV epidemic control with the prevalence reported at 1.5% (1.8% females and 1.1% Males) 15 years and above. There are however still challenges with the identification of all HIV positives and initiation on treatment standing at 81.8% and 89.5% though the viral load suppression is better at 92.5% against UNAIDs targets of 95:95:95. With the commitment of the Ministry of Health, support of development partners, 85 out of 101 facilities have been coded. There are more temporary facilities in locations hosting South Sudanese refugees which would not fit the criteria for transition. Efforts are ongoing to develop district transition plans and national transition guidelines to guide and fast track transition of health facilities to the MOH and district local government. All locations were able to continue to hold settlement-level coordination meetings with the co-leadership of the district and the involvement of the different partners.

projects.description:
Advocacy and engagement in the review and reform of legislation and policies.
WFP’s advocacy initiatives in collaboration with the Uganda Parliamentary Forum on Social Protection and the Ministry of Gender Labour and social Development contributed to the re-instating of the Senior Citizen’s Grant budget for financial year 2023/2024 from 20% to 100% worth USD 26.4 million.  Other advocacy priorities were on increased financing for Social Protection including fast tracking the 4th Northern Uganda Social Action Fund (NUSAF4) Project, expansion of coverage of civil and national identification registration and the first of a kind Social Protection Week from 27th October to 3rd November 2023 under the theme “Investing in social protection across the lifecycle”.

projects.name: Food insecure populations in areas affected by recurring climate shocks have access to adequate and nutritious food all year
projects.description: WFP aims to ensure food-insecure populations in climate-affected areas have year-round access to adequate and nutritious food. Through its livelihood and resilience-building programme, WFP provided technical assistance to the Government and supported men and women to establish community assets while strengthening the national social protection system for livelihood and resilience programs. Under the school feeding programme, WFP provided nutritious school meals to improve education access, retention, and learning outcomes, while offering technical support to the Government to foster national ownership. These efforts align with Uganda’s Third National Development Plan (NDP III) and aim to establish a sustainable, government-led Home-Grown School Feeding (HGSF) model which focuses on procuring food locally from SHFs to enhance community resilience and support local food systems. (ACL/SRM & HGSFP)

projects.name: Provide technical and financial support for Restoration and Management of Wetland Hydrology and Associated Catchments.
projects.description:
At country level, the Programme is designed to contribute to sustainable natural resource management, ecosystem and community resilience to climate change and livelihood improvement. The main objective is to protect, restore and maintain the integrity of degraded fragile ecosystems and increasing the country's resilience to impacts of climate change. The programme implementation started in 2018 and is expected to end in 2026. Specifically, the outcomes anticipated out of these efforts include:
1) Restoration and management of wetland hydrology and associated catchments
2) Improved agricultural practices and alternative livelihood options in the wetland and catchment
3) Strengthening access to climate and early warning information to farmers and other communities to support wetland management.
projects.outcome: Output 2.2.1: Strengthened capacity of public and private institutions and communities to sustainably manage natural resources and protect vital ecosystems

projects.name: 3.1.1.6 Provide technical and financial assistance to government and non-government actors to increase access  to gender inclusive and equitable health services including SRH, Mental Health, NCD prevention and control for all especially vulnerable and marginalised.
projects.description:
UNHCR
Achievements: In the Health Sector, the Under-5 mortality remained below the standard of <1.5/1,000. Mosquito net distribution, Indoor residual spraying (iRS) as well as Integrated community case management (iCCM) have ensured that mortalities are contained. Measles vaccination coverage was (83%) against the standard of 95% mainly due to vaccine stockouts as well as the increased number of new refugees. The consultations per clinician per day were higher for the Congolese (DRC) population (65) than for the South Sudan (SSD) population (40) than the acceptable standard of 50 consultations per clinician per day. During the reporting period, the health partners have identified and treated 7,874 children and 2,662 pregnant and lactating women for acute malnutrition, with a cure rate of 71.5%. The Refugee Population-based HIV Impact Assessment (RUPHIA) revealed the gains in HIV epidemic control with the prevalence reported at 1.5% (1.8% females and 1.1% Males) 15 years and above. There are however still challenges with the identification of all HIV positives and initiation on treatment standing at 81.8% and 89.5% though the viral load suppression is better at 92.5% against UNAIDs targets of 95:95:95. With the commitment of the Ministry of Health, support of development partners, 85 out of 101 facilities have been coded. There are more temporary facilities in locations hosting South Sudanese refugees which would not fit the criteria for transition. Efforts are ongoing to develop district transition plans and national transition guidelines to guide and fast track transition of health facilities to the MOH and district local government. All locations were able to continue to hold settlement-level coordination meetings with the co-leadership of the district and the involvement of the different partners.

projects.name: 3.1.1.1 Provide technical and financial support to government and non government actors to expand and sustainably provide  high impact food security and nutrition interventions for vulnerable and marginalised population especially adolescents and women of reproductive age in development and humanitarian situations
projects.description:
UNHCR
UNHCR
Achievements: The food security sector continues to contribute to Strategic Development Goal 2.1 by improving access to nutritious food among refugees and asylum seekers in the 13 refugee settlements in Uganda. Furthermore, the sector promotes the self-reliance of refugee communities through complimentary activities. The partners reached 1.39 million beneficiaries through the provision of in-kind food as well as cash-based transfers by the end of Q2. However, owing to the prioritization exercise conducted in July 2023, there was a reduction of 14% of beneficiaries who received in-kind assistance and 6% reduction in cash assistance. Additionally, the further reduction in in-kind rations in most refugee settlements due to limitations in funding increased cash enrolments since beneficiaries preferred cash to the reduced rations. Overall, the proportion of beneficiaries who received cash assistance increased from 60% to 63% from Q1 to Q4. 
Digital cash transfer mechanisms through agent banking continued to be scaled up, and cash beneficiaries owning bank accounts increased from 36 percent to 41 percent out of the overall total cash beneficiaries by the end of the year. To increase access to digital payment instruments, Mobile money will start in Kyangwali and Kiryandogo settlements. In addition to increasing access to digital payment instruments through agency banking, cash beneficiaries received financial literacy skills. A total of 2,954 beneficiaries were trained during the reporting period across all 13 settlements. Efforts to mitigate malnutrition continue to be strengthened through building the capacity of health workers, Village Health Teams (VHTs), and other community structures in providing Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) knowledge to promote better household nutrition. Similarly, active case findings have supported in managing the nutrition situation in the settlements. Currently, the recovery rate remains above the threshold with an average of 93% discharged as cured from the programme within the reporting period.

projects.name: Enhancing Conjunctive Management of Surface and Groundwater Resources in Selected Transboundary Aquifers: Case Study for Selected Shared Groundwater Bodies in the Nile Basin
projects.description:
The project aims to attain more effective utilization and protection of selected shared aquifers in the selected sub-basin in the Eastern Nile and the Nile Equatorial Lakes region through further improving the understanding of available groundwater resources and demonstrating ‘conjunctive management’ that optimizes the joint use of surface and groundwaters. The project is focusing on three transboundary aquifers, namely:
•	Gedaref-Adigrat Aquifer (between Ethiopia and Sudan), 
•	Kagera Aquifer (covering parts of Burundi, Rwanda, Tanzania and Uganda) and
•	The Mt Elgon Aquifer (between Kenya and Uganda).

projects.name: 3.1.1.6 Provide technical and financial assistance to government and non-government actors to increase access  to gender inclusive and equitable health services including SRH, Mental Health, NCD prevention and control for all especially vulnerable and marginalised.
projects.description:
UNHCR
Achievements: In the Health Sector, the Under-5 mortality remained below the standard of <1.5/1,000. Mosquito net distribution, Indoor residual spraying (iRS) as well as Integrated community case management (iCCM) have ensured that mortalities are contained. Measles vaccination coverage was (83%) against the standard of 95% mainly due to vaccine stockouts as well as the increased number of new refugees. The consultations per clinician per day were higher for the Congolese (DRC) population (65) than for the South Sudan (SSD) population (40) than the acceptable standard of 50 consultations per clinician per day. During the reporting period, the health partners have identified and treated 7,874 children and 2,662 pregnant and lactating women for acute malnutrition, with a cure rate of 71.5%. The Refugee Population-based HIV Impact Assessment (RUPHIA) revealed the gains in HIV epidemic control with the prevalence reported at 1.5% (1.8% females and 1.1% Males) 15 years and above. There are however still challenges with the identification of all HIV positives and initiation on treatment standing at 81.8% and 89.5% though the viral load suppression is better at 92.5% against UNAIDs targets of 95:95:95. With the commitment of the Ministry of Health, support of development partners, 85 out of 101 facilities have been coded. There are more temporary facilities in locations hosting South Sudanese refugees which would not fit the criteria for transition. Efforts are ongoing to develop district transition plans and national transition guidelines to guide and fast track transition of health facilities to the MOH and district local government. All locations were able to continue to hold settlement-level coordination meetings with the co-leadership of the district and the involvement of the different partners.

projects.name: Support Building transformative policy and financing frameworks to increase investments in biodiversity management (BIOFIN) in Uganda
projects.description:
By 2025, Uganda's natural resources and environment are sustainably managed, protected and people especially the vulnerable and marginalized - have the capacity to mitigate and adapt to climate change and disaster risks. The main focus of this Programme is to 
1) Develop a biodiversity Index to inform Ecological Fiscal Transfer (EFT) Mechanisms.
2) Support the initiation of Payment for Ecosystem Services (PES) Programme to enhance the use of economic instruments as incentives for biodiversity conservation and management.
3) Initiate piloting of eco-tourism and eco-tourism and eco-enterprises for wetlands and Ramsar Sites in Cities and Municipalities in Uganda.
4) Engagement of youth and women in conservation to support conservation of biodiversity.
projects.outcome: Output 2.2.1: Strengthened capacity of public and private institutions and communities to sustainably manage natural resources and protect vital ecosystems

projects.name: 3.1.1.1 Provide technical and financial support to government and non government actors to expand and sustainably provide  high impact food security and nutrition interventions for vulnerable and marginalised population especially adolescents and women of reproductive age in development and humanitarian situations
projects.description:
UNHCR
UNHCR
Achievements: The food security sector continues to contribute to Strategic Development Goal 2.1 by improving access to nutritious food among refugees and asylum seekers in the 13 refugee settlements in Uganda. Furthermore, the sector promotes the self-reliance of refugee communities through complimentary activities. The partners reached 1.39 million beneficiaries through the provision of in-kind food as well as cash-based transfers by the end of Q2. However, owing to the prioritization exercise conducted in July 2023, there was a reduction of 14% of beneficiaries who received in-kind assistance and 6% reduction in cash assistance. Additionally, the further reduction in in-kind rations in most refugee settlements due to limitations in funding increased cash enrolments since beneficiaries preferred cash to the reduced rations. Overall, the proportion of beneficiaries who received cash assistance increased from 60% to 63% from Q1 to Q4. 
Digital cash transfer mechanisms through agent banking continued to be scaled up, and cash beneficiaries owning bank accounts increased from 36 percent to 41 percent out of the overall total cash beneficiaries by the end of the year. To increase access to digital payment instruments, Mobile money will start in Kyangwali and Kiryandogo settlements. In addition to increasing access to digital payment instruments through agency banking, cash beneficiaries received financial literacy skills. A total of 2,954 beneficiaries were trained during the reporting period across all 13 settlements. Efforts to mitigate malnutrition continue to be strengthened through building the capacity of health workers, Village Health Teams (VHTs), and other community structures in providing Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) knowledge to promote better household nutrition. Similarly, active case findings have supported in managing the nutrition situation in the settlements. Currently, the recovery rate remains above the threshold with an average of 93% discharged as cured from the programme within the reporting period.

projects.description:
UNHCR
Achievements: In the Health Sector, the Under-5 mortality remained below the standard of <1.5/1,000. Mosquito net distribution, Indoor residual spraying (iRS) as well as Integrated community case management (iCCM) have ensured that mortalities are contained. Measles vaccination coverage was (83%) against the standard of 95% mainly due to vaccine stockouts as well as the increased number of new refugees. The consultations per clinician per day were higher for the Congolese (DRC) population (65) than for the South Sudan (SSD) population (40) than the acceptable standard of 50 consultations per clinician per day. During the reporting period, the health partners have identified and treated 7,874 children and 2,662 pregnant and lactating women for acute malnutrition, with a cure rate of 71.5%. The Refugee Population-based HIV Impact Assessment (RUPHIA) revealed the gains in HIV epidemic control with the prevalence reported at 1.5% (1.8% females and 1.1% Males) 15 years and above. There are however still challenges with the identification of all HIV positives and initiation on treatment standing at 81.8% and 89.5% though the viral load suppression is better at 92.5% against UNAIDs targets of 95:95:95. With the commitment of the Ministry of Health, support of development partners, 85 out of 101 facilities have been coded. There are more temporary facilities in locations hosting South Sudanese refugees which would not fit the criteria for transition. Efforts are ongoing to develop district transition plans and national transition guidelines to guide and fast track transition of health facilities to the MOH and district local government. All locations were able to continue to hold settlement-level coordination meetings with the co-leadership of the district and the involvement of the different partners.

projects.name: 3.1.1.6 Provide technical and financial assistance to government and non-government actors to increase access  to gender inclusive and equitable health services including SRH, Mental Health, NCD prevention and control for all especially vulnerable and marginalised.
projects.description:
UNHCR
Achievements: In the Health Sector, the Under-5 mortality remained below the standard of <1.5/1,000. Mosquito net distribution, Indoor residual spraying (iRS) as well as Integrated community case management (iCCM) have ensured that mortalities are contained. Measles vaccination coverage was (83%) against the standard of 95% mainly due to vaccine stockouts as well as the increased number of new refugees. The consultations per clinician per day were higher for the Congolese (DRC) population (65) than for the South Sudan (SSD) population (40) than the acceptable standard of 50 consultations per clinician per day. During the reporting period, the health partners have identified and treated 7,874 children and 2,662 pregnant and lactating women for acute malnutrition, with a cure rate of 71.5%. The Refugee Population-based HIV Impact Assessment (RUPHIA) revealed the gains in HIV epidemic control with the prevalence reported at 1.5% (1.8% females and 1.1% Males) 15 years and above. There are however still challenges with the identification of all HIV positives and initiation on treatment standing at 81.8% and 89.5% though the viral load suppression is better at 92.5% against UNAIDs targets of 95:95:95. With the commitment of the Ministry of Health, support of development partners, 85 out of 101 facilities have been coded. There are more temporary facilities in locations hosting South Sudanese refugees which would not fit the criteria for transition. Efforts are ongoing to develop district transition plans and national transition guidelines to guide and fast track transition of health facilities to the MOH and district local government. All locations were able to continue to hold settlement-level coordination meetings with the co-leadership of the district and the involvement of the different partners.

projects.name: 3.1.1.1 Provide technical and financial support to government and non government actors to expand and sustainably provide  high impact food security and nutrition interventions for vulnerable and marginalised population especially adolescents and women of reproductive age in development and humanitarian situations
projects.description:
UNHCR
UNHCR
Achievements: The food security sector continues to contribute to Strategic Development Goal 2.1 by improving access to nutritious food among refugees and asylum seekers in the 13 refugee settlements in Uganda. Furthermore, the sector promotes the self-reliance of refugee communities through complimentary activities. The partners reached 1.39 million beneficiaries through the provision of in-kind food as well as cash-based transfers by the end of Q2. However, owing to the prioritization exercise conducted in July 2023, there was a reduction of 14% of beneficiaries who received in-kind assistance and 6% reduction in cash assistance. Additionally, the further reduction in in-kind rations in most refugee settlements due to limitations in funding increased cash enrolments since beneficiaries preferred cash to the reduced rations. Overall, the proportion of beneficiaries who received cash assistance increased from 60% to 63% from Q1 to Q4. 
Digital cash transfer mechanisms through agent banking continued to be scaled up, and cash beneficiaries owning bank accounts increased from 36 percent to 41 percent out of the overall total cash beneficiaries by the end of the year. To increase access to digital payment instruments, Mobile money will start in Kyangwali and Kiryandogo settlements. In addition to increasing access to digital payment instruments through agency banking, cash beneficiaries received financial literacy skills. A total of 2,954 beneficiaries were trained during the reporting period across all 13 settlements. Efforts to mitigate malnutrition continue to be strengthened through building the capacity of health workers, Village Health Teams (VHTs), and other community structures in providing Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) knowledge to promote better household nutrition. Similarly, active case findings have supported in managing the nutrition situation in the settlements. Currently, the recovery rate remains above the threshold with an average of 93% discharged as cured from the programme within the reporting period.

projects.name: 3.1.1.6 Provide technical and financial assistance to government and non-government actors to increase access  to gender inclusive and equitable health services including SRH, Mental Health, NCD prevention and control for all especially vulnerable and marginalised.
projects.description:
UNHCR
Achievements: In the Health Sector, the Under-5 mortality remained below the standard of <1.5/1,000. Mosquito net distribution, Indoor residual spraying (iRS) as well as Integrated community case management (iCCM) have ensured that mortalities are contained. Measles vaccination coverage was (83%) against the standard of 95% mainly due to vaccine stockouts as well as the increased number of new refugees. The consultations per clinician per day were higher for the Congolese (DRC) population (65) than for the South Sudan (SSD) population (40) than the acceptable standard of 50 consultations per clinician per day. During the reporting period, the health partners have identified and treated 7,874 children and 2,662 pregnant and lactating women for acute malnutrition, with a cure rate of 71.5%. The Refugee Population-based HIV Impact Assessment (RUPHIA) revealed the gains in HIV epidemic control with the prevalence reported at 1.5% (1.8% females and 1.1% Males) 15 years and above. There are however still challenges with the identification of all HIV positives and initiation on treatment standing at 81.8% and 89.5% though the viral load suppression is better at 92.5% against UNAIDs targets of 95:95:95. With the commitment of the Ministry of Health, support of development partners, 85 out of 101 facilities have been coded. There are more temporary facilities in locations hosting South Sudanese refugees which would not fit the criteria for transition. Efforts are ongoing to develop district transition plans and national transition guidelines to guide and fast track transition of health facilities to the MOH and district local government. All locations were able to continue to hold settlement-level coordination meetings with the co-leadership of the district and the involvement of the different partners.

projects.name: 3.1.1.6 Provide technical and financial assistance to government and non-government actors to increase access  to gender inclusive and equitable health services including SRH, Mental Health, NCD prevention and control for all especially vulnerable and marginalised.
projects.description:
UNHCR
Achievements: In the Health Sector, the Under-5 mortality remained below the standard of <1.5/1,000. Mosquito net distribution, Indoor residual spraying (iRS) as well as Integrated community case management (iCCM) have ensured that mortalities are contained. Measles vaccination coverage was (83%) against the standard of 95% mainly due to vaccine stockouts as well as the increased number of new refugees. The consultations per clinician per day were higher for the Congolese (DRC) population (65) than for the South Sudan (SSD) population (40) than the acceptable standard of 50 consultations per clinician per day. During the reporting period, the health partners have identified and treated 7,874 children and 2,662 pregnant and lactating women for acute malnutrition, with a cure rate of 71.5%. The Refugee Population-based HIV Impact Assessment (RUPHIA) revealed the gains in HIV epidemic control with the prevalence reported at 1.5% (1.8% females and 1.1% Males) 15 years and above. There are however still challenges with the identification of all HIV positives and initiation on treatment standing at 81.8% and 89.5% though the viral load suppression is better at 92.5% against UNAIDs targets of 95:95:95. With the commitment of the Ministry of Health, support of development partners, 85 out of 101 facilities have been coded. There are more temporary facilities in locations hosting South Sudanese refugees which would not fit the criteria for transition. Efforts are ongoing to develop district transition plans and national transition guidelines to guide and fast track transition of health facilities to the MOH and district local government. All locations were able to continue to hold settlement-level coordination meetings with the co-leadership of the district and the involvement of the different partners.

projects.name: 3.1.1.6 Provide technical and financial assistance to government and non-government actors to increase access  to gender inclusive and equitable health services including SRH, Mental Health, NCD prevention and control for all especially vulnerable and marginalised.
projects.description:
UNHCR
Achievements: In the Health Sector, the Under-5 mortality remained below the standard of <1.5/1,000. Mosquito net distribution, Indoor residual spraying (iRS) as well as Integrated community case management (iCCM) have ensured that mortalities are contained. Measles vaccination coverage was (83%) against the standard of 95% mainly due to vaccine stockouts as well as the increased number of new refugees. The consultations per clinician per day were higher for the Congolese (DRC) population (65) than for the South Sudan (SSD) population (40) than the acceptable standard of 50 consultations per clinician per day. During the reporting period, the health partners have identified and treated 7,874 children and 2,662 pregnant and lactating women for acute malnutrition, with a cure rate of 71.5%. The Refugee Population-based HIV Impact Assessment (RUPHIA) revealed the gains in HIV epidemic control with the prevalence reported at 1.5% (1.8% females and 1.1% Males) 15 years and above. There are however still challenges with the identification of all HIV positives and initiation on treatment standing at 81.8% and 89.5% though the viral load suppression is better at 92.5% against UNAIDs targets of 95:95:95. With the commitment of the Ministry of Health, support of development partners, 85 out of 101 facilities have been coded. There are more temporary facilities in locations hosting South Sudanese refugees which would not fit the criteria for transition. Efforts are ongoing to develop district transition plans and national transition guidelines to guide and fast track transition of health facilities to the MOH and district local government. All locations were able to continue to hold settlement-level coordination meetings with the co-leadership of the district and the involvement of the different partners.
